title: Audio library
summary: Recordings of papers and books, verbatim or summarized, to listen to anywhere.
description: Papers read aloud: verbatim, a whole paper or any of its sections, or a summary of several. Recordings are made once, on any device, and sync to all of them for listening offline, on a phone with the screen off.

requirements.text: The audio library holds recordings of the library's papers and books, newest first; each opens in a player.
The author can record an item verbatim, whole or one of its sections from its contents, down to the smallest; the sections within a recording are its chapters.

A verbatim recording reads the text as written. Formulas are said the way a mathematician reads them aloud, and figure captions are read; the bibliography, page numbers, running heads and footnote marks are not.
The author can record a summary of one or more items, read by one narrator, at a length from `audio.summary-lengths`; the summary's parts are its chapters.

Recordings are spoken by `audio.speech-model` through OpenRouter, in a voice the author picks, and their text is prepared by `audio.script-model`; both can be changed in Settings, and their use is logged in the ledger.

A recording is made on any device, in the background while the app runs, and shows how far it has come; if the app stops, it carries on from where it was without speaking again what was already spoken.
Recordings are kept as Opus in WebM, mono at `audio.bitrate`, and sync to every device for listening offline.
The player plays, pauses, seeks, skips between chapters, and plays at a speed from `audio.speeds`.
Where the author stopped listening is kept and syncs, so a recording carries on from there on any device.
On a phone, a recording keeps playing with the screen off and the app in the background, with lock-screen, notification and headphone controls, which skip between chapters too.
On a computer, the keyboard's media keys control the player.
The player's address holds the recording and the moment playing, `#t=<seconds>`.
